Question B-001-016-007.

Why the correct answer is right: Single sideband is prohibited in the 10.100 MHz to 10.150 MHz band.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "18.068 MHz to 18.168 MHz": This range sits in the 7 MHz to 25 MHz group with a 6 kHz limit, rather than in the special 10.100 MHz to 10.150 MHz band where SSB is prohibited.
- sourceIndex 2: "24.890 MHz to 24.990 MHz": This range is another 7 MHz to 25 MHz HF choice governed by the 6 kHz group limit, not by the special SSB-prohibited 10.100 MHz to 10.150 MHz rule.
- sourceIndex 3: "7.000 MHz to 7.300 MHz": This is the 40-metre band; ordinary SSB voice is about 2 kHz to 3 kHz wide and fits within a 6 kHz HF limit, so it is not the special SSB-prohibited band.
